mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and HOUST drops by more than 10% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in average hourly earnings growth (proxied by PAYEMS growth), signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of sustained unemployment above 4.0% and negative average hourly earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing that boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 2% for three months) combined with a concurrent rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals pent-up demand and inflationary pressure, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 2% for 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during episodes of high savings growth and elevated CPI.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 3.5% for five consecutive months, regardless of other macro conditions, signals persistent labor market weakness that depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of five consecutive months with UNRATE above 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion that boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month AND > +1% AND HOUST > previous month AND > +1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with INDPRO and HOUST both rising by more than 1%.
